extraFactQuestions.claim: Your payslip must state the name of your chosen super fund and the dollar amount contributed.
extraFactQuestions.why: Fair Work Regulation 3.46 requires the name (or name and number) of the fund the contribution was made to. That can be a default fund, not one the employee chose, so 'chosen' narrows the rule. The word was in the original text, so I left it.

extraFactQuestions.claim: Full-time employees accrue 4 weeks (152 hours) of annual leave per year, equal to 2.923 hours per week.
extraFactQuestions.why: 152 hours and 2.923 hours per week assume a 38-hour week. The figures are typed into the text and not derived from a constant. Shift workers under some awards accrue 5 weeks.

factQuestions.claim: residents benefit from the $0 tax-free threshold
factQuestions.why: The resident tax-free threshold is $18,200 (taxed at 0%), not $0. The intended wording is probably 'the 0% rate on the $18,200 tax-free threshold'. I left it because changing it would change a number.

factQuestions.claim: Non-residents also cannot access ... the Medicare levy exemption benefit that residents receive.
factQuestions.why: This contradicts line 103, which says non-residents are fully exempt from the Medicare levy. Residents do not receive a levy exemption. The point is probably that non-residents lose Medicare benefits (bulk billing, PBS), as the line 143 bullet explains.

factQuestions.claim: No Medicare levy exemption (bullet heading in the list of benefits non-residents lose)
factQuestions.why: Non-residents ARE exempt from the levy. The bullet body actually describes losing access to Medicare services. The bold heading (locked) is misleading and should be something like 'No Medicare access'.

factQuestions.claim: No tax-free threshold costs up to {formatAUD(TAX_FREE_THRESHOLD * SECOND_BRACKET_RATE)} in additional tax at the 15% marginal rate
factQuestions.why: A non-resident pays 30% (NR[0].rate) on the first $18,200 where a resident pays 0%. That makes the extra cost TAX_FREE_THRESHOLD * NR[0].rate, not * SECOND_BRACKET_RATE. The current formula understates it by half.

factQuestions.claim: Both employees receive superannuation at 12% ($10,800)
factQuestions.why: The figures are hard-coded rather than taken from SUPER_GUARANTEE.rate. Also, line 122 calls the person an 'IT contractor', and a genuine contractor is not automatically owed SG. The example should say employee.

factQuestions.claim: This exemption saves a non-resident earning $100,000 a total of $2,000 per year compared to a resident without private health insurance.
factQuestions.why: The 2% Medicare levy is payable whether or not a resident has private health insurance (insurance only affects the surcharge), so that qualifier is misleading. The $2,000 is also hard-coded rather than calculateMedicareLevy(100_000).

factQuestions.claim: Non-residents can claim a 'Foreign Income Tax Offset' (FITO) in their home country for Australian tax paid, or claim an offset in Australia for tax paid overseas
factQuestions.why: FITO is Australia's own offset; a home country gives its own foreign tax credit. Also, non-residents are not taxed in Australia on foreign income, so they generally have no Australian FITO claim.

factQuestions.claim: A non-resident receiving dividends from an Australian company typically faces a withholding rate of 15% under most DTAs, reduced from the standard 30% domestic rate.

factQuestions.claim: Worked example Step 5: the employee's RFBA on the income statement is $10,401, the Type 1 grossed-up amount.
factQuestions.why: Reportable fringe benefits amounts are always grossed up at the Type 2 rate. The constants file says the same: 'grossUpType2 ... also used for ALL reportable amounts'. On a $5,000 taxable value the RFBA would be $5,000 x 1.8868 = $9,434, not $10,401.

factQuestions.claim: Rates table: the reportable fringe benefits threshold is '$2,000 grossed-up taxable value'.
factQuestions.why: The ATO test is a total taxable value over $2,000 (not grossed up). The grossed-up minimum is $3,773 (FBT.reportableMinimumGrossedUp). Line 43 states it correctly. Line 215 ('$2,000 grossed-up threshold') and the table cells at lines 99-100 ('Yes, if grossed-up value > $2,000') have the same problem.

factQuestions.claim: Employer-paid health insurance is a Type 1 benefit.

factQuestions.claim: Car base value is the 'GST-inclusive cost price minus any dealer delivery charges already exempt'.

factQuestions.claim: pre-16 August 1978 service is taxed at a flat 5%, while post-1978 service is taxed at 32% (up to the whole-of-income cap)
factQuestions.why: ATO rules: for pre-16 Aug 1978 service, 5% of the amount is included in assessable income and taxed at marginal rates, so it is not a flat 5% tax. 16 Aug 1978 to 17 Aug 1993 service is taxed at a maximum 32%. Post-17 Aug 1993 service is taxed at marginal rates unless the termination is a genuine redundancy. The whole-of-income cap applies to ETPs, not to unused long service leave.
factQuestions.constant: Text; ideally a termination-tax constant shared with the long-service-leave calculator

factQuestions.claim: The ATO uses a strict multi-factor test ... It depends on the working arrangement (e.g., control over work, providing your own tools, bearing financial risk), not just what your contract says. "Sham contracting" penalties apply to employers who get this wrong.

Sham contracting under s 357 also has a reasonable-belief defence, so 'apply to employers who get this wrong' oversimplifies it.

factQuestions.claim: A standard civil penalty under the Fair Work Act is up to 60 penalty units per contravention for individuals and 300 for companies, and serious contraventions attract up to ten times that.

factQuestions.claim: Annual leave payouts are taxed as ordinary income at the employee's marginal tax rate. The ATO does not apply any concessional treatment to annual leave payouts. ... the pre-16 August 1978 component is taxed at 5%, and the post-1978 component is taxed at the marginal rate.
factQuestions.why: ATO rules: unused annual leave accrued before 18 Aug 1993, or paid out in a genuine redundancy, invalidity or approved early retirement, is taxed at a maximum of 30% plus Medicare levy. For long service leave, only 5% of the pre-16 Aug 1978 amount is added to assessable income (it is not taxed at a 5% rate), and the 16 Aug 1978 to 17 Aug 1993 portion is capped at 30% plus Medicare levy. The leave-calculator.tsx tax note also says long service leave 'may qualify for concessional tax treatment', which contradicts this paragraph.
factQuestions.constant: Unused leave payment tax rules (ATO 'Unused leave payments on termination') should sit in a tax constants file, e.g. lib/constants/australian-tax.ts

The intro says the table covers weekday overtime, so the Sunday column's basis (ordinary hours or overtime) is unclear. The Hospitality public holiday rate for full-time staff is 225%, not 250%.
